finding: Eastern U.S. timber losses to disturbance
what_it_says: Timber value lost to insects, disease, fire, weather, and other disturbances rose from about $30.8 billion a year (decade ending 2015) to about $49.5 billion a year (decade ending 2024)
source: Wear and Coulston 2026, Resources for the Future Working Paper 26-10

what_it_says: Fell about 17% from 1990 to 2023 (about 1,049 to 873 million metric tons CO2e a year, forest land remaining forest land)
source: EPA Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks 1990 to 2023, chapter 6

what_it_says: Hold about 20% more aboveground carbon, including standing dead trees, than unprotected forests
source: Faison et al. 2023, Forest Ecology and Management 544:121145

what_it_says: Managing some forests intensively for wood, others more lightly, and setting aside reserves could raise carbon uptake 15% to 25% with no loss of harvest
source: Daigneault, Simons-Legaard and Weiskittel 2024, Forest Policy and Economics
